abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between CEO and top executive ownership and the choice between secured and unsecured debt financing. Although prior research has found that debt structure affects agency costs and firm value, the relationship between executive ownership and debt preferences remains open to debate. We find that an increase in executive ownership results in a higher percentage increase in the use of secured debt, which may be attributed to the managerial effort-enhancing behaviour that results from collateralized debt. Additionally, we find that firms in financial distress tend to rely more heavily on secured debt. Our results contribute to understanding how managerial incentives influence capital structure decisions and the determinants of debt security choices.
authors: Vivek Bhargava Mukesh Chaudhry Daniel Huerta Thanh Ngo a Lutgert College of Business
Lucas Institute for Real Estate Development & Finance
title: Executive ownership and the choice between secured and unsecured debt
title_zh: 高管持股与担保债务与非担保债务的选择

abstract: Government digitalization has emerged as a key strategy for streamlining regulatory processes and improving public service delivery, yet its impact on the private sector remains unclear. Utilizing novel data from private firms, we examines the effect of China’s ‘Internet Plus Government Services’ reform, which integrates Internet technologies into public service provision, on private firm creation. We find that digital government significantly promotes entrepreneurship in the private sector by enhancing information accessibility and increasing administrative efficiency. The effect is more pronounced for smaller firms and in regions with higher institutional quality and greater Internet penetration. Moreover, digital government fosters high-quality private entrepreneurship, leading to increased job creation and enhanced innovation. These findings underscore the role of digital government as a catalyst for economic growth and innovation in the private sector.
